findings.title: Dropping the +50 turns round-to-nearest into floor, so customers get less discount and pay more
findings.body: The old code `Math.floor((amount * percent + 50) / 100)` rounded to the nearest minor unit, with an exact half rounded up. The new `Math.floor((amount * percent) / 100)` always rounds the discount down. For 10% off 1999 the discount is now.

contracts.action: percentageDiscount now floors instead of rounding half up
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous implementation of the same function, which added 50 before dividing by 100. The documented rule is in discount.ts:10-18 and docs/features/discounts.md:9-12.
contracts.before_after: Before: discount = floor((amount*percent+50)/100), round to nearest with half up. After: discount = floor(amount*percent/100), always rounds down. Callers coupon.ts:65 and promotion.ts:38 pass the result straight on as the discount amount.
contracts.visible_effect: Percentage coupons and percentage line promotions give up to 1 minor unit less discount, so the cart total goes up by that amount (for example 1800 instead of 1799 for 10% off 1999).
contracts.failure_mode: No error is raised. The total is silently wrong against the documented rule, and discount.test.ts:16-21 fail.

summary: The one-line change drops the `+ 50`, so percentage discounts round down instead of to nearest with half up. That contradicts the docstring, `docs/features/discounts.md` and `discount.test.ts`, and.
